## D-075 · Three roles on `memberships`, read from the row on every request, never from a claim · **Added 2026-09-29 (tenant management Phases 1–3). Reverses D-041**

**Decision:** `memberships.role` is `owner | admin | staff` (every row that
existed became `admin`, what D-041 said a row meant). `app_role()` reads it
inside Postgres; `app_is_admin()` keeps its name and now means owner or
admin, so the thirty policies that name it changed meaning without an
edit; `app_is_staff()` (any member) is asked only by the six bookings and
unanswered policies. In code, `staffClient()` returns the same row's role,
`requireAdmin(request, tenant, permission)` refuses with a 403 that names
the role and the permission, and `lib/permissions.ts` is the ONE table of
what each role may do: owner everything plus members; admin the knowledge
base, rooms, rates, photos, holidays and bookings; staff bookings and
unanswered, the knowledge base read-only. A staff token carries `sub` and
`app_admin`, as before, and NO role: a demotion, like a removal, takes
effect on the next request. The request's names (`BUSINESS_OWNER` …)
became `owner | admin | staff`, because the row's `tenant_id` already says
"business", and the screens label them Owner, Admin, Staff (§ 8 q1).

**Why:** the user asked for role-based access. D-041 named the reversal
condition ("staff who can see bookings but not edit documents") and the
route ("add `role`, make `app_is_admin()` role-aware"), and that is what
was done. Reading the role from the row rather than a claim is what lets
a token never outrank the database.

**Measured:** verify 109/109 (a staff token cannot insert a document, an
admin can; a staff token inserts and reads a booking; an owner changes a
role in its tenant only, 1 row, and staff or a cross-tenant update 0);
staff-cases 13/13 ("Your role (staff) may not do this (documents:write)…",
bookings 200, rooms 403, documents read 200); `permissions.test.ts` pins
the roles `can()` grants for each of twelve permissions to the roles the
policies let through, listed by hand from `schema-roles.sql`.

**Reverse if:** a tenant needs a role between these (a "front desk" that
confirms requests but does not create bookings). Add the value to the
check constraint, a row to `ROLE_PERMISSIONS`, and a line to the test; the
policies need no change unless the new role's writes cut across
`app_is_admin()` / `app_is_staff()`.

## D-076 · The platform is a table and a second, tenant-less token shape; it manages every tenant's record and reads no tenant's content · **Added 2026-09-29 (tenant management Phases 1–4). Amends D-039 and D-042, and CLAUDE.md rule 8**

> **Amended 2026-10-14 by D-128:** the platform now reads, adds and deletes a tenant's knowledge-base documents and chunks (`documents_super_all`, `chunks_super_all`). It still reads no booking, guest, message or payment.

**Decision:** a super user is a `platform_admins` row, not a membership.
`mintPlatformToken({ userId })` mints `{ role: authenticated, sub,
app_super: true }` with NO `tenant_id`, from the same signer as the tenant
token, still with no role parameter and still five minutes. With no tenant
claim, every tenant policy is false for it; the `*_super_*` policies on
`tenants`, `tenant_applications` and `memberships` open those three
tables, and each asks `app_is_super()`, the claim AND the row, on every
read and write. It has its own cookie (`rag_platform`, path
`/api/platform`, payload kind `platform`), its own area (`/platform`), and
its own routes under `withPlatformRoute()`. To open a tenant's screens a
super user makes itself an owner there, one click on the members panel
(§ 8 q5), and from then on it is an ordinary staff session.

**Why:** "a super user is an owner of every tenant" fails on the token: a
staff token names a tenant, and the platform's work (list, create) has none
yet. A separate shape keeps the two lanes provable: a platform cookie at a
tenant route is a 401, a tenant cookie at the platform is a 401, and the
platform reads 0 documents, chunks and bookings while managing every
record. `tenants` gets its first policy, and it is false for every token
but this one.

**Measured:** verify: a platform token with its row lists all tenants
(count = service_role's) and 0 documents, chunks and bookings; the same
token with the row deleted lists 0 tenants; the pipeline isolation suite
21/21: villa's context on a platform token reads 0, 0, null, null through
the routes' own functions; the Phase 4 walk 12/12; the bundle holds
neither `app_super` nor `platform_admins` nor `rag_platform` nor any key
value. Five unit tests pin both shapes' claim lists.

**Reverse if:** the platform ever needs to read tenant content (support
staff reading a chat). Do not widen the token; make the super user an
owner of that tenant, which is what "Make me an owner" is for.

## D-077 · Archive, not delete, in the browser; hard delete is the CLI's, and it sweeps Storage · **Added 2026-09-29 (tenant management Phases 1, 2, 5). § 8 q7's rule for applications**

**Decision:** the platform form archives (`tenants.archived_at`) and
unarchives. `tenant_public()` adds one clause, `archived_at is null`, so
every page, route and chat of an archived tenant answers 404 at once,
while the platform still reads it by id. Nothing is deleted. Hard delete is
`tenant:remove -- <slug> --yes`: it prints thirteen counts, insists on
`--yes`, cascades, then runs `storage-orphans -- --remove` and reports the
count. Switching an application off is refused by a trigger while a
booking has not ended, and the rows stay for when it comes back.

**Why:** `tenants` cascades to bookings (names, phones, emails) and to
`unit_images` rows, whose Storage objects do not cascade (R-30). A Delete
button is one click from all of that; a command that prints what it is
about to take and sweeps after is the right distance.

**Measured:** `tenant:remove` on `cli-probe` and `probe-tm`: the counts,
the cascade through both new triggers (the last-owner and no-delete-live
guards let a cascade through because the tenants row is already gone), the
sweeper reporting 2 objects with their 2 rows and no orphans; the walk:
archived → page, admin and chat 404, platform GET 200, unarchive → 200.

**Reverse if:** a real tenant asks for its data to be deleted from the
browser. Then a two-step confirm on the form that names the counts, still
never on the same click as archive.

That is a column on `units`, and `request_booking()` would take the

## D-079 · One permission table, two walls: every admin route names its permission, and Postgres asks the same role again · **Added 2026-09-29 (tenant management Phases 1, 3, 6). Extends D-038**

**Decision:** `lib/permissions.ts` holds twelve permissions for three
roles, pure enough for the browser to import. `requireAdmin()`'s third
argument is REQUIRED, so a route that forgets does not compile (D-027's
argument applied to roles), and a 403 names the role and the permission (a
member already knows the tenant exists, so "not yours = not there" does not
apply). The screens hide by `can()` and decide nothing. Behind every route
the policies ask `app_is_admin()` or `app_is_staff()`, and
`permissions.test.ts` pins the two views to each other permission by
permission, by hand. Three permissions the plan did not list exist so that
every GET names an honest one: `session`, `rooms:read`, `holidays:read`.

**Why:** D-038's rule, each wall tested alone, applied to permissions. A
permission only the code knows is a wall nobody tests; a permission only
Postgres knows is a 42501 with no sentence a person can act on.

**Measured:** typecheck listed all 31 call sites when the argument became
required; staff-cases 13/13 over HTTP; verify 109/109 in SQL; 17 web
tests.

**Reverse if:** never wholesale. A permission moves between roles by
editing the table, the policy and the test together, and the test fails
until all three agree.

## D-080 · A closed date is a holiday-calendar row, and closed is closed: nothing pending or confirmed lands on it, from anyone · **Added 2026-09-30 (closed dates)**

**Decision:** a date the business is not operating is a `rate_calendar`
row with `kind = 'closed'` and no surcharge. It closes the WHOLE property
for every slot that starts on that date; a single room is taken out by
making it inactive, as before. Staff set it on the Holidays screen
(admins and owners, the calendar's existing policies).
- **Wall 2, Postgres** (`schema-closed-days.sql`): `bookings_not_on_closed_day`
  refuses any insert, or any move into `pending` or `confirmed`, on a
  closed date. That covers staff bookings, `request_booking()` and a
  staff confirm alike. `rate_calendar_closed_check` refuses to close a
  date that has confirmed bookings, and says how many. Both take one
  advisory lock per tenant first, so a closure and a booking cannot both
  pass their checks at once (write skew).
- **Wall 1, the code** (`@rag/bookings`, `closed.ts`): every write path
  says why before it writes, in the same words the trigger's refusal is
  mapped to. Every availability read reports the date as `closed`, so the
  Bookings screen, the booking page and the chatbot's tool all say so.
- **The chatbot's tool TEXT is unchanged.** A closed date is explained in
  the tool RESULT (`closed: { dates, meaning }`), and only when a row is
  closed. Dates only: the label staff typed is not put into a prompt.
- **No SQL function was replaced.** The `closed` status is applied in
  `checkAvailability()` and `pricedAvailability()`, not in
  `check_availability()` or `check_room_availability()`. So no older file
  needs a guard (CLAUDE.md trap 20), and the ten definer functions stay
  ten.

**Why:** the user's four answers, 2026-09-30: whole property; refuse to
close a date with confirmed bookings; no staff override; the chatbot says
"closed". The calendar already had the right shape (one row per tenant
and day, for every unit, read by any token, written by admins), so a new
table would have repeated its policies. Pending requests do not block a
closure because they hold nothing (D-070); they cannot be confirmed, and
staff decline them.

**Measured:** rooms 34/34 (30–33 new). The same raw insert is refused on
a staff token and on service_role, and a raw `request_booking()` on a chat
token is refused too, so the trigger holds alone. Its twin books the day
after.
- **Where the chatbot learns it, measured three ways on `rt-leak-2`**
  ("Is the Garden Room free?" asked of villa). The original text passed
  3 of 4. With "closed" in the description, 1 of 4. With the description
  and an instruction line, 0 of 6, and the model invented "the Garden Room
  is part of the whole property".
- **The result note instead.** With the text unchanged and no note, a
  closed villa date was listed under "Taken:" (3 of 3). With the note,
  villa said "closed on 16 March 2027" 3 of 3 and harbor 2 of 2, and the
  open day after was answered as open each time. The tool definitions are
  byte-identical to both baselines, and so is northwind's prompt.

**Reverse if:** a tenant needs to close one room on a date, not the whole
property. That is a `unit_id` on the closure, and it changes every check.

  on `slots` (insert / update / delete, tenant + `app_is_admin()`, like

unless `{ retired: true }` (the bookings and requests lists, whose rows

`pricedAvailability()` leave retired slots' rows out; the staff booking,

## D-091 · A list in a reply is a pipe table, drawn by ONE hand-written parser into elements, never into HTML · **Added 2026-10-04 (plan/tables.md)**

**Decision:** room lists, room details, availability, prices and the
extra-guest terms are presented as a table. The chat recognises exactly
ONE block syntax, a GitHub pipe table (a header line over a `|---|`
separator), parsed by `apps/web/lib/tables.ts` (pure, no dependency,
never throws) into segments that `components/reply-text.tsx` renders as
`<table>` with every cell a React CHILD. Nothing else is parsed: no bold,
links, headings or lists, and `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` stays absent. A
block without the separator is text; a short row is padded, a long one
cut; a row still streaming is text until its closing `|` lands. Three
writers share the shape: `packages/rag/src/tables.ts` (`pipeTable()`) for
the replies code writes (`roomListReply()`, D-087; the rate card for an
undated price, amending D-081; the extra-guest terms handed to the model),
and the instruction lines in `tools.ts` and `dates.ts` for the model's
own, each an example of what TO write (D-017). Rule 4: a one-room or
one-slot question is a sentence; a table of the other open rooms may
follow it. The rate kind is named once in the sentence, not in every cell
(D-082 amended). On a phone each row is a card with the column names in
front (`data-label`). No tool definition and no base prompt changed:
northwind's prompt and both tool definitions are byte-identical to their
baselines.

**Why:** the user: "present them as a table format". A markdown library
would have turned every reply into markup, which is the one thing the chat
has refused since the POC (textContent, never innerHTML); one block shape,
parsed into elements, keeps that rule and gives the table. The model
could not be trusted to write the shape every time, so the replies code
writes are guaranteed, and the model's are measured.

**Measured (plan/tables.md Phases 0–4, one day):** web tests 46 (15
parser, 4 component); pipeline 351. Phase 3's first run (52/61) found two
checks stricter than Rule 4 and one regression, `rt-leak`, 0 of 3 with the

## D-095 · A booking is born pending; staff confirm it, and confirming is what takes the span · **Added 2026-10-04. Extends D-070 to staff bookings**

**Decision:** `createBookings()` (and `createBooking()`, which calls it)
inserts `pending` unless the caller names a status; the staff route's
schema has no `status` key (zod strips one), so a booking made on the
Bookings screen is pending. `confirmBooking(tenant, id)` (`@rag/bookings`)
moves pending → confirmed, the WHOLE group in one statement for a
several-rooms booking; `PATCH /api/t/<slug>/bookings/[id]` with
`{ action: 'confirm' }` calls it, and the screen's row shows **Confirm**
beside Cancel while pending. `sql/schema-pending-default.sql` (the 16th
file, run by the user) sets the column default to `pending`, the second
wall: a raw insert naming no status is pending too. A pending row holds
nothing (D-070), so confirmation is the moment the span is taken, and a
clash is the 409 `bookings_no_overlap` raises there, in the server's own
words; a closed date is refused in words. The tools that seed test
bookings (the battery's two fixtures, isolation, rooms) pass
`status: 'confirmed'` explicitly, because a seeded booking must take its
night. Existing rows do not change.

**Why:** the user: "Booking created by a staff should not be
automatically confirmed." The same rule a customer's request already
had, now for staff: nothing is held until someone says so.

**Cost, stated:** until confirmed, a staff booking leaves the date OPEN to
the chatbot, the booking page and other staff, exactly as a request does.
Confirm promptly, or the span can be taken by another confirmed booking,
and Confirm then answers 409. **Amended by D-099 (2026-10-05):** once a
night is confirmed, no further pending booking can be created on it from
any door (a trigger), and a pending one already there is flagged `clash`
on the list and refused at Confirm.

**Measured:** tests 99/355/56; typecheck; rooms **40/40** (4b new: born
pending, a second pending allowed on the same night, Confirm takes the
whole group → `confirmed,confirmed`, the second's Confirm is a
`BookingConflictError`, a chat token cannot confirm); bookings isolation
30/30 both ways (the "same slot again is a 409" check had to seed
confirmed: with no status it quietly created a pending row, twice, and
both were deleted by id); battery **57/61**, the known set, `tool 9/9`,
both fixtures seeded confirmed. Owed to the user: run the SQL file, and
the screen walk (create → "pending" with Confirm → confirmed).

**Decision:** a `promos` table per tenant (name; `kind` fixed or percent;

over the STAY dates; an optional code, unique per tenant ignoring case; an
optional usage limit; active) and two columns on `bookings`, `promo_id`
and `discount`. The discount is `promo_discount()`'s and nothing else's
(Rule 1): a fixed amount on the FIRST row of a stay, capped at that
night's price, a percentage on every row rounded half up (q5); the insert
trigger stores it and `price` net of it, `request_booking()` resolves a
typed code under the tenant's request lock and stores every night's
share, and the two quotes preview the same rows in the same order. A
customer reaches a promo only through `promo_for_request()`, security
definer (Rule 2): the promo for a typed code with a reason when it does
not apply ('dates', 'exhausted'), or the automatic one with the largest
discount for this stay, and nothing for a wrong or another tenant's code;
`promos` has no policy for a chat token. Uses are `count(distinct
request)` pending or confirmed, computed never stored (§ 2.3), and the
limit is checked under the lock on both doors (Rule 3): a staff booking
counts (q2). A stored discount never changes (Rule 4); a used promo is
retired, never deleted. Tenant-wide for now (q4). `promos:read` /

percentage … validity date range … requires promo code? … limit of usage
… only 10 customer can avail". Every number a visitor or a receipt shows
already came from one SQL function per night and one per stay; a
discount computed anywhere else would be the first second copy of a

## D-099 · A pending booking cannot be born on a span that is already confirmed; the staff list says which pending rows would clash · **Added 2026-10-05 (plan/staff-clash.md). Amends D-095's cost line**

**Decision:** one BEFORE INSERT trigger, `bookings_pending_not_taken`
(`sql/schema-taken-span.sql`, the 20th file), refuses a `pending` row
whose unit and span overlap a `confirmed` row of the same tenant, with
`23P01` (the exclusion constraint's own code, so every map to 409 holds
unchanged) and words that name the date and the unit: "taken on
2026-10-20: Garden Room is already confirmed for that slot". It runs as
the caller with `search_path = ''`, named to fire after
`bookings_compute_during` so it reads a computed span, and refuses a null
span rather than passing it (trap 12). `taken.ts` is the ONE place the
trigger's `23P01` is told apart from the constraint's: the trigger's words
pass through to the caller, the constraint's text still gets the
package's sentence. `listBookings()` carries `clash` on a pending row
whose date, unit and slot are confirmed for another row, the Requests
section's definition; the Bookings screen shows that section's warning
under such a row and disables its Confirm, Cancel enabled. The screen is
the courtesy and the server the guard (trap 21): a stale tab's Confirm
still meets `bookings_no_overlap`'s 409.

**What stands:** D-070 and D-095. A pending row still holds nothing:
`bookings_no_overlap` is untouched, two pending rows may still share a
night (§ 7 q2), the first one confirmed takes it, and the other's Confirm
is the 409 it was. The trigger only stops a pending row being BORN on a
night someone already holds. No lock (Rule 4): an insert that reads "no
confirmed row" while a concurrent Confirm commits leaves a pending row
beside a confirmed one, which is exactly what `clash` names and what
Confirm then refuses; the window is one statement wide.

**D-095's cost line, amended:** "until confirmed, a staff booking leaves
the date OPEN … Confirm then answers 409" now reads: a pending booking
leaves the date open to be CONFIRMED by someone else, and once it is, no
further pending booking can be created on it from any door, and the one
already there is flagged and refused at Confirm.

**Learned (Phase 1):** the customer's door was SQL-guarded already:
`request_booking()` checks the confirmed rows itself and raises `23P01`
"That date is no longer available" before any insert, so the trigger
stands behind that check. The staff door had no SQL check; the trigger is
its wall 2.

**Why:** the user: "i can still book a room/slot that was already taken
using staff booking. or this is intentional?" It was D-095's stated cost,
and the Requests section already warned where the staff list did not.

## D-100 · Every stay is a group with one reference, whoever made it; the Requests section decides every pending stay · **Added 2026-10-05 (plan/staff-requests.md)**

**Decision:** `booking_reference(p_tenant_id)` (`sql/schema-staff-requests.sql`,
the 21st file) is the ONE place a reference's shape is written: three
letters of the slug, six from a 30-letter alphabet, retried while a row
of the tenant has the result; security definer (the twelfth, D-042's
shape), because `tenants` has no policy for a token, and it checks its
caller first: the token's own tenant, `service_role`, or a direct session
(`session_user = 'postgres'`, where the backfill runs). `request_booking()`
calls it instead of its inline loop (the promos file's definition is
guarded on this file's marker, trap 20). A BEFORE INSERT trigger,
`bookings_aa_fill_group_and_reference`, gives a row its own `group_id`
when the insert names none and the group's `reference` when a row of the
same statement already set one, else a new one, so a several-rooms staff
booking gets ONE reference; a counted backfill gave every older row both.
`listRequests()` and `decide()` read every source: the Requests section
lists every pending stay, web or staff, labelled "from the booking page"
or "by staff", with the same Confirm and Decline (one group, one
statement, the same 409 and closed-date words); `source` is on the
request, and `groupSize` on the list row, so "group booking" means
several rows, not "has a group". The staff list keeps its own Confirm
(q4). D-070, D-095 and D-099 stand untouched: a pending row holds
nothing, is born pending, cannot be born on a confirmed night, and
Confirm takes the span.

**Why:** the user: "why staff created booking doesnt have a reference
number?" and "why staff created booking dont show up on 'Requests'
section on top". A reference existed only where `request_booking()` made
one, and the Requests section listed only what had a group. One shape
for a stay removes both special cases, and the reference lives in one
function the way every price lives in `unit_quote()`.

**Learned:** a volatile function in an UPDATE's SET is evaluated once per
ROW. The first backfill wrote `set reference = booking_reference(…)` and
harbor's one 2-room staff booking got two references, found by the Phase
2 HTTP smoke (the trigger was right; rooms 4f proved one reference per
2-room insert). The file now calls the function into a variable first,
and a repair step keeps the lowest id's reference on a split group. The
first run of the file rolled back whole because the function refused the
SQL editor's own session; a definer's `current_user` is its owner, so the
LOGIN role, `session_user`, is what tells a direct session from
PostgREST's `authenticator`.

## D-102 · Feedback, load and empty states, search, tabs and tips are five small components, still hand-written · **Added 2026-10-08 (plan/ui-components.md)**

**Decision:** the staff screens share five components instead of each
screen doing it its own way. All are in `apps/web/components/`, with no
library (D-101's rule).
- `toast.tsx`: `useNotice(drawerOpen)` keeps `setNotice()`'s signature. A
  success is a toast that leaves after 5 s. A refusal while the drawer is
  open stays in the drawer. Any other refusal is a toast that stays until
  closed. There is ONE queue per tab and ONE `<Toaster />` per page,
  rendered by `StaffFrame` and the platform screen, and it is a
  `popover="manual"` element in the top layer, so it sits above modals.
- `load-state.tsx`: `LoadState`, a skeleton while loading, or an alert with
  Retry that runs the load that failed; and `EmptyState`, a title, a line
  and the page's own add button, or none for a role that may not add.
- `list-search.tsx` with `lib/search.ts`: a search over the rows already
  loaded, plus "Show more", 25 at a time.
- `tabs.tsx`: the WAI-ARIA tabs pattern, every panel kept mounted.
- `tooltip.tsx`: `Tip`, shown on hover AND keyboard focus, closed by
  Escape, hoverable (WCAG 1.4.13). No HTML element keeps a native `title`.

The rule this sets: a TOAST says what an action did; a `.notice` BANNER
says a standing fact (an overlap, a closed date, a contrast warning).

**Why:** the user asked for an audit of reusable UI components, and took
every recommendation. The dialog and the drawer existed already (D-101).
What did not:
- Action feedback appeared at the top of the page, off-screen after a row
  action, and under an open drawer.
- A failed load looked exactly like a slow one, and had no retry.
- Empty lists pointed at a button elsewhere on the page.
- 200 unanswered questions had no search.
- The platform's tenant form was one long page.
- Reasons were kept in `title`, which a keyboard, a phone and a screen
  reader never see.

**Learned:**
- A modal `<dialog>` hides everything beneath it, so a page-level message
  needs the top layer too, which is what `popover` gives.
- Two panels on one page (the platform's form and its members) need ONE
  region, or their toasts stack in the same corner. A module queue also
  lets a message outlive the component that raised it.
- A legend beats ~112 focusable chips.
- CDP's `keyDown` needs `text: "\r"` to press a button.

**Measured (2026-10-08, `feat/ui-refresh`):** walks: Phase 1 20/20,
Phases 2–3 44/44, Phase 4 14/14, Phase 5 9/9, Phase 6 12/12. Every write
was caught in the browser, so nothing changed. Tests 13+14+102+359+5+85.
The axe audit (0 on 160 states) was last run after Phase 1; the user
asked that it and `pnpm eval` wait for their word.

## D-105 · Booking, payment and change requests are three statuses; payment and `completed` are derived, `expired` is stored · **Added 2026-10-10 (plan/manage-booking.md)**

**Decision:** `bookings.status` gains `expired` only. The PAYMENT status is
`stay_payment()`'s, derived from `payments` every time it is asked
(`not_tracked | unpaid | submitted | rejected | partially_paid | paid |
refunded`), with `required`, `received` (verified payments minus verified
refunds), `outstanding` and `enough`. `completed` is a confirmed stay whose
last night has ended, derived (`guestStatus()`). Change requests are their
own table with their own status. A stay is a GROUP (D-100), so `stays` holds
its reference and its terms (`required_amount`, `pay_by`, `review_by`);
`required_amount` is computed ONCE, when a web stay is born, by
`stay_required()` (a percentage rounds UP), so a settings change never moves
a guest's goalposts. Staff stays are not tracked.

**Why:** the request's own warning: one status column would tangle "is it
confirmed?", "is it paid?" and "did they ask to move?". A column nobody
writes cannot disagree with what produced it.

**Measured:** verify 133–136, 143; walk 3, 6/6.

## D-106 · A hold is per tenant (`none` / `on_proof` / `on_request`), a flag the constraint reads, released before every write · **Added 2026-10-10 (plan/manage-booking.md § 2.4, § 9 q1). Amends D-070 for tenants that opt in**

**Decision:** `config.payments.hold`, default `none` (every tenant today):
D-070, D-095, D-099 stand exactly. `on_proof` holds a stay's nights from its
proof until `review_by`; `on_request` holds a web stay from birth until
`pay_by`. The mechanism (`schema-holds.sql`, the 24th file):
`bookings.held` + `held_until`; `bookings_no_overlap` becomes `where (status
= 'confirmed' or held)`; `booking_takes()` is the ONE taken test every read
asks (confirmed, or held and not lapsed, using `now()`); lapsed holds are
released before an insert and a Confirm; a row leaving pending drops its
hold. `check_availability()`, `check_room_availability()`,
`request_booking()` and `bookings_pending_not_taken()` were re-made with
`booking_takes()` (the last also says "is held for another guest", which
`taken.ts` passes through), and their older copies and the constraint's are
GUARDED on `booking_takes()` (trap 20).

**Why:** a constraint cannot compare with `now()`, so the hold is a flag; a
lapsed flag still in the table must block nothing, so reads use the time and
writes clear the flag first. No job is needed for correctness (pg_cron is
available, not enabled). `on_request` is the request's preference but lets
anyone with a phone number block dates, D-070's reason; `on_proof` holds from
the moment someone has plausibly paid.

**Measured:** verify 145–150; with `none` every tenant's availability
(2026-10-10 to +30) and the three prompt baselines byte-identical to Phase 0;
battery 55/61, the three new misses with identical tool results (trap 24).

## D-108 · Cancel and reschedule are requests; approval inserts the new nights in the same stay in one transaction · **Added 2026-10-10 (plan/manage-booking.md § 2.8, § 9 q5)**

**Decision:** a guest ASKS (`request_change()`, a dry run first for the
quote; `withdraw_change()`); owners and admins DECIDE (`decide_change()`).
One open request per stay. The policy is per tenant: refund tiers by days
before check-in (`change_terms()`: a percentage of what was RECEIVED, rounded
down) and a reschedule cutoff. A reschedule keeps the rooms, slot, nights and
guests and moves the dates; no promo is carried. Approving it cancels the old
nights and inserts the new ones in the SAME group under `request_booking()`'s
lock, so the reference holds; a night taken meanwhile is 23P01 and nothing
changes. A dearer stay's difference becomes the outstanding balance by itself
(stay_payment() sums the live rows). Approving a cancel cancels the stay and
keeps the refund due on the request; staff pay and record it.

**Why:** the request: keep the original reservation until the change is
secured; never promise a refund by cancelling.

**Measured:** verify 151–156; walk 6, 4/4.

## D-116 · Staff hear what waits on them: in the app, and on their devices by Web Push · **Added 2026-10-14 (schema-notifications.sql, schema-notification-reads.sql)**

**Decision:** three things that wait on staff are news:
- a guest's booking request (`created`, by a guest, pending; one per
  stay);
- a proof of payment (`payment:submitted`);
- a guest's change request (`<kind>:pending`).

The `booking_events` log is the ONE source (Rule 1). An AFTER INSERT
trigger, `booking_events_notify`, writes a `notification_outbox` row in
the event's transaction, and no route "also sends a push". Staff-made
stays, decisions, the expiry sweep and refunds are not news (plan § 7 q3).

**Two layers:**
- **In the app:** every open staff tab polls `GET /admin/attention` every
  30 s, hidden or not (§ 8 reversed § 2b.9's pause). A new arrival is a
  toast and a two-tone `OscillatorNode` chime; the sound is on unless the
  device turned it off, and is woken by the first click or key in a tab.
- **Web Push:** VAPID (RFC 8292) and `aes128gcm` (RFC 8291), hand-written
  in `@rag/push` over `node:crypto` (§ 7 q6). It equals RFC 8291
  Appendix A byte for byte, so `web-push` was not needed. There is no
  Firebase: each browser's own push service delivers.
  - **Subscribing:** a member subscribes a device per tenant from the
    sidebar, with per-kind boxes (§ 7 q9). One service worker per
    tenant, scope `/t/<slug>/`, and a per-tenant manifest for iPhone's
    Home Screen.
  - **Sending:** the drain is `notify_claim()` → `sendPush()` →
    `notify_done()`, run with `after()` behind the guest's response and
    swept by the staff poll (§ 7 q5).
  - **Recipients:** decided from the membership row at send time
    (Rule 3). A request or change reaches every role; a proof reaches
    owners and admins only (`NOTIFY_PERMISSION`, tested against the SQL).

**S-17 Notifications (§ 8, the user's walk on 2026-10-14):**
- The sidebar has ONE badge: what this member has not READ, on every
  device at once (`notification_reads`). Bookings and Payments carry none.
  Phase 1 had badged them with what WAITS, which only deciding could
  lower, so opening a notification never cleared a number.
- The list is the last 30 days, in the push's own words. Opening a row,
  or tapping its push (the outbox id is in the payload), marks it read.
  "Mark all read" clears the rest.
- `notification_feed()` and `notification_read()` are security invoker
  and refuse non-staff. Staff read their tenant's outbox under the push's
  role rule.

**Payload (Rule 2):** kind, reference, first night, nights, path and
outbox id. Never a guest's name, phone, email or amount (§ 7 q4); a lock
screen shows it, and the push service is a third party.

**Secrets (Rule 4):** `VAPID_PRIVATE_JWK` is read in ONE function,
`vapidKeys()`, which is `server-only`. Unset, push is off and says so,
and the in-app layer still works. The public key reaches the browser from
`GET /admin/push`, not as a page prop. That is a deviation, because
threading one non-secret string through every staff screen was not worth
it.

**Not done, on purpose:**
- email (§ 7 q7: the outbox can gain a channel);
- guests notified of anything;
- custom push sounds (the OS chooses, § 2b.5);
- a cron drain (§ 7 q5: revisit at deployment).

**Measured:**
- verify **187** (173–186);
- bookings isolation **40/40** both ways (31a–g);
- RFC 8291's vector byte for byte; the build's static files clean of
  every secret by name and by value;
- walks: Phase 4 5/5 off and on, Phase 5 4/4 in two real Chrome profiles
  (Google accepted both pushes 3–4 s after the response), inbox 12/12 (a
  hidden tab chimed 28 s after a request), sound 5/5 (and on the old code
  it fails as reported), devices 4/4;
- axe: 8 states, 0 violations;
- the three chatbot baselines byte-identical.

**Owed:** the phone walk (Android with Chrome closed; iPhone from the Home
Screen), gated on deployment or a tunnel (§ 7 q8).

## D-128 · What each role may do is set per tenant, on the platform · **Added 2026-10-14. Amends D-075, D-076 and D-079**

**Decision:** `lib/permissions.ts`'s table stays as the DEFAULT. A super user
changes it per tenant on the platform form's Permissions tab, stored as
`role_permissions` rows (`sql/schema-role-permissions.sql`, the 34th file):
- any CONFIGURABLE permission can be taken from a role (18 of 21);
- a GRANTABLE one can also be given to a role that lacks it (documents,
  rooms, holidays, slots and promos);
- three are FIXED: session, payments:write and payments:settings.

`can(role, permission, overrides)` in code and `app_can()` in SQL compute
the same answer from the same rows, and `permissions.test.ts` pins the two
lists and the default matrix to the SQL file. The super user may also manage
a tenant's knowledge base from the platform (a Knowledge base tab; super
policies on `documents` and `chunks`).

**Why:** the user asked for role permissions configured on the platform,
with the example "only the super user uploads knowledge-base documents; the
owner only reads". That is two rows (owner and admin lose documents:write)
plus the platform's own upload.

**Why not everything is grantable:** a permission checked inside a SECURITY
DEFINER function (verify a proof, payment settings) or a trigger that names
a role (members) cannot be widened by a row: one wall would allow what the
other refuses. Restricting is always safe, because a RESTRICTIVE policy is
ANDed with what exists.

**How:** the existing policies are untouched, so no older file needed a
guard. Each gained a restrictive twin (`<table>_may_<cmd>`, through
`app_may()`, which passes any non-member token), and each grantable one a
permissive twin (`<table>_can_<cmd>`).

**Found on the way:** the first version also restricted promos' SELECT on
promos:read. That is the Promos SCREEN, admin-only by default, but the
database lets every member read promos for the staff form's picker. verify
198's positive twin caught it, and the policy was removed.

**Code-only (stated, not hidden):** dashboard:read, conversations:read and
the rooms/holidays/slots reads guard screens over data that every token of
the tenant can already read (the chat reads rooms, slots and every message).
Withholding them is wall 1's job; Postgres keeps its old rule for that data.

## D-132 · Staff notes on a stay: many per stay, append and delete your own · **Added 2026-10-15**

**Decision:**
- A stay has any number of staff notes (`stay_notes`, `sql/schema-stay-notes.sql`, the 36th file), on S-15's **Staff notes** card. They are for staff: never on Manage booking, never in a prompt or a tool result.
- Read with `bookings:read`, add with `bookings:write`, through `app_can()` in the policies themselves, so D-128's per-tenant overrides reach them with no twin policy.

- The author is the token's user: the column default, and the insert policy demands it.
- Retention (D-131): a note may hold guest details, so a trigger deletes a stay's notes when its guest is removed. `remove_guest_details()` is not replaced (traps 20, 25).

**Why not reuse `bookings.notes`:** that is one text per ROW, written on the booking form and repeated on every night; a log of many dated, attributed entries is a table.

## D-133 · A room is a TYPE with physical rooms; every count is rows, and Postgres assigns the room · **Added 2026-10-20 (plan/room-types.md). Amends D-034 and D-070**

**Decision:**
- `units` stays the room TYPE: its name, capacity, rates, photos and promos, so no price changes (`unit_price()`, `unit_quote()`, `promo_discount()` untouched). Under it, `unit_rooms` (`sql/schema-room-inventory.sql`, the 37th file) holds the physical rooms: `id, tenant_id, unit_id, name, active, sort_order`, unique `(unit_id, name)`, a composite foreign key to its unit's tenant. Every unit was backfilled with one room named like it, so every tenant behaved as before until staff added a second.
- `bookings.room_id` is `not null`, and `bookings_no_overlap` is per room (D-034 amended).
- ONE assigner, `bookings_room_assign`, a BEFORE INSERT trigger after `compute_during`, picks the room under an advisory lock on (tenant, unit) when an insert names none: the room the same group used the night before, then the first free by `sort_order`, preferring one with no pending row. It is every door's: the booking page, staff, `decide_change()`'s reschedule, the tools. Confirm re-picks (BEFORE UPDATE) when the room was taken meanwhile (`schema-room-counts.sql`, the 38th).
- The count is ALWAYS active rows, never a quantity column. Availability (`check_availability`, `check_room_availability`) carries `rooms_free` and `rooms_total`; `taken` means 0 free. `request_booking()` takes a type several times up to its free rooms, signature unchanged.
- Staff move a stay between rooms of its type: `move_room()` (definer, `bookings:write`, a note required, a `booking_events` row of kind `room`), and `bookings_room_move_guard` refuses a retired or taken room in words, raw updates too (`schema-room-move.sql`, the 39th). The price never moves.
- The calendar counts rooms ("1 of 2") and the dashboard's occupancy is over rooms (`schema-room-views.sql`, the 40th).
- A whole-resort unit keeps one active room (a trigger). A room ever booked is retired, never deleted (the D-090 pattern).
- Guests see a count, never a room number: the booking page says "1 of 2 left" and caps its count by the quote's `free`; the tool row carries `left: "1 of 2"` for an open type of several rooms only, in the RESULT, never the tool text (the three baselines byte-identical; `closedNote()`'s precedent, D-080). Manage booking shows the type (§ 7 q4).

**Why rows and not a `quantity`:** a number typed beside the rows can disagree with them; a booking needs a room to sit in for the constraint to refuse a loser (trap 8), and staff need a room to move.

**Why the assigner in SQL:** every door inserts; one trigger under a lock is the only place two concurrent requests cannot both pick the last room, and the constraint still refuses the loser.

**Not done:** merging alteza's Kubo A and Kubo B into one type (the owner's call, § 7 q1); a guest choosing a room number.

## D-134 · Voice: speech in and speech out around the unchanged pipeline · **Added 2026-10-20 (plan/voice.md)**

**Decision:**
- A guest may speak a question and hear the answer on the chat. A recording becomes text on the server (`POST voice/transcribe`, OpenAI transcription, `transcribe()` in `@rag/openai`), the browser sends that text to `chat/` exactly as if it had been typed, and the complete reply is read aloud (`POST voice/speak`, `speak()`). Between the two nothing changes: no prompt, tool, `language.ts` or `dates.ts` text, and a spoken question is stored as its words.
- The speak route takes a `conversationId`, never text: an open route that spoke any text would be free text-to-speech on the tenant's key. It reads the conversation's latest reply through `latestReply()` on the chat token (both walls), the refusal marker as the tenant's words, and speaks `speakable()` of it (`apps/web/lib/speakable.ts`: no markers, emoji or addresses; a table as its first column's names and "the details are on your screen"; at most 600 characters).
- When OpenAI's speech fails, stalls past 15 s or is refused, the browser reads the SAME `speakable()` text with a voice of its own, but only a `localService` one; with none, silence (Rule 6, added at the user's word after Phase 0). A failed transcription asks the guest to type; the question has no browser fallback (Firefox has none, Chrome's sends audio to Google).
- No recording is kept: in memory to OpenAI and dropped. The notice under the field and the tenant's privacy page say so when voice is on.
- A feature switch, `voice`, OFF with no row (the only one; `defaultOn: false` in `lib/features.ts`, `tenant_feature_on()` in `schema-voice.sql`, the 41st file), because it adds cost and a third party. A spoken question's answer is always read; a typed one's when the guest turns on "Read replies aloud".
- Every recording carries a `prompt` hint, `transcriptionHint(businessName)`: the business and "Filipino (Tagalog), English, or a mix of both (Taglish)". No `language`, which would force one. Added after the user's walk heard short Tagalog as Malay ("Kenapa perlu sama ada") with no hint. Since the second walk ("Casa Uno" heard as "pasauna") it also names the tenant's active rooms and slots, at most 20 (`voiceVocabulary()`, on the chat token, filtered on the tenant).
- `OPENAI_TTS_MODEL` defaults to `tts-1`: Phase 0 measured `gpt-4o-mini-tts` at 116 s of OpenAI's own processing and `tts-1` at 1.1 to 1.9 s to the first byte.

**Why not speech-to-speech (Realtime):** the model would answer from the audio, past `buildPrompt()`, so the grounding, the refusal, the tools and the battery would not apply.

**Why after the reply, not while it streams:** the speak route reads only what is stored (above). A spoken reply starts about 2 s after the text is complete.

## D-137 · The per-IP limit is ONE count in Postgres, on every open route, the chat included · **Added 2026-10-20 (plan/rate-limit.md). Closes R-39; amends R-13 and R-53**

**Decision:**
- The per-IP window on the open routes leaves `lib/rate-limit.ts`'s in-memory `Map` for ONE table, `rate_windows`, and ONE `security definer` function, `rate_allow(p_tenant_id, p_key, p_max, p_window_seconds)` (`sql/schema-rate-limit.sql`, the 42nd file; the thirteenth callable definer). It bumps the key's current window and judges it in ONE statement (`insert … on conflict do update … returning count`), so two instances bumping the same key at once both see the true count; there is no "read, then write" (trap 8). The window is `date_bin(window, now(), a fixed origin)`, so every instance bins alike.
- Two walls (D-038): the key carries the tenant id, and the function refuses an id that is not the token's `app_tenant_id()`. `rate_windows` has no policy for any token; the function is the only way to it.
- `allow(tenant, key, max?)` is async over that function and keeps every caller's key, number and 429 sentence. The database down THROWS, so the route 500s through the one error map: no fallback count, no fail-open.
- **The chat route is limited** for the first time: 30 turns per address per tenant per 10 minutes, checked after validation and before the Accept header is read, so a refused turn is one JSON 429 in both deliveries and nothing is spent. A greeting answered in code counts too.
- **A per-tenant ceiling across addresses** on the routes that spend OpenAI money (the chat and the two voice routes): `allowSpend()` checks the address's window, then `<scope>|<tenant>|*` at 600 per 10 minutes, bumped only for an allowed address. It is what a caller rotating addresses meets (R-53).
- The numbers (10, 30, 600, 10 minutes) are policy, not measurements, each in one constant in `lib/rate-limit.ts` (voice's 30 stays in `lib/voice.ts`).
- The function sweeps the TENANT's windows older than two windows on every call (`rate_windows_sweep_idx`), so a one-off visitor's row is gone the next time anyone on that tenant is counted. Nothing here is a person's data for longer than twenty minutes; `retention` is not involved.
- `lib/rate-limit.ts` has no `server-only` marker, on purpose: it holds no secret and no client (it is handed the tenant's), and leaving it off is what lets vitest load it.
- Out: `book/quote` and the room-list reads (no model behind them), the staff routes (behind a login Supabase throttles), an audit log (R-13's other half).

**Why:** the user asked whether the code is production ready. The shared limit was one of four things owed before a public URL, and the only one that needs no deployment: the voice routes had only the per-instance window behind their OpenAI spend (R-53) and the chat had nothing.

**Observed:** verify 229/229 (225–229: ten inside and the eleventh out with ONE row at count 11; another tenant's id is `42501`; a chat token reads nothing from the table while the service client sees the rows; a row aged three windows is swept by the next call; keys apart). `plan/rate-limit-walk.mjs` 8/8 over HTTP on villa from a fresh address per run: 30 chats 200 then the 31st 429 in words, the table at 31 and the ceiling row at 30; a second address fresh; the ceiling seeded at 600 refuses a new address and makes no conversation; a streamed request past the limit is one JSON 429; `book/request` ten 400s then 429 and `manage` ten 404s then 429, unchanged words, each table row at 11. `plan/voice-phase2-walk.mjs` 6/6 (its 31st transcribe call 429). Web tests 202 (9 new), every package green, typecheck 13/13, rooms 56. No file under `packages/rag` changed; villa's tool definitions byte-identical to `villa-tools-post-villa-prices.txt`.

**Learned:** the first draft swept per KEY; a visitor who never returned would have kept their row forever. The sweep is per tenant, with its own index. The chat screen needed no change: its catch already reads a response's own `error` through `describeFailure()`.

## D-138 · An audit log: who did what, as staff and as a super user, written by Postgres alone · **Added 2026-10-20 (plan/audit-log.md)**

**Decision:**
- ONE append-only table, `audit_log` (`sql/schema-audit-log.sql`, the 43rd file). A row is who (`actor_kind` staff, super or system; `actor_user`), when, the area, the action, the row's key and label, the NAMES of the changed columns, and before/after of a short allowlist per table. No token has an insert, update or delete policy on it.
- Postgres writes it, never a route: `audit_row()`, ONE trigger function with ONE `case` on the table, is attached to the 16 tables a staff or platform token may change (documents on insert and delete only: an edit is a new id, D-044); `audit_note()`, a definer, writes exactly three named actions, `login`, `logout` and `proof_opened`, and refuses a token with no user first, so a chat token can never write a row and a failed login is not a row (Supabase keeps those).
- One event, one table: bookings, stays, payments and change requests keep `booking_events`; the trigger is not on them, so no guest's name, phone, email or amount enters `audit_log`. `activity_list()`, `security invoker`, reads both sources into one list, the stay's reference and statuses only, never its note.
- Who reads: `activity:read`, an owner's by default and grantable to admins (D-128; both lists in the 34th file and the code). The read policy is the tenant's rows with the permission, every row for a super user (the log holds no guest and no content, so D-076's line is not crossed); the function refuses the wrong caller itself as well. A super user's action on a tenant shows on the tenant's screen as "Platform", unnamed.
- A tenant's hard delete cascades through every audited table; the trigger skips a delete whose tenant is already gone (the first run failed every probe tenant's delete on the FK), and `tenant:remove` writes the one platform row, `tenant_removed`, itself on service_role: the only insert outside the trigger and the definer.
- Retention: `tenants.audit_retention_days` (730 by default, 90 to 3650, on the platform's Legal tab); the `retention` tool deletes past it, counted, and the platform's own rows after 730 days.
- S-18 `/t/<slug>/admin/activity` (Setup, after Members), the platform tenant form's Activity tab, and a Platform activity card on `/platform`: ONE list component, ONE words module (`lib/activity-words.ts`), the filters (window, area, one person, a search over the label) in the URL on S-18.
- The chatbot is untouched: no prompt text, no tool text, villa's and alteza's snapshots byte-identical to Phase 0, villa's tool definitions to their baseline.

**Why:** every action but a booking's existed only as a console line the dev server printed and nobody kept (R-13, since 2026-09-20). A log written by the database cannot be forgotten by a route and cannot name another actor.

**Why the platform's view of a tenant has no stay log:** the platform token has no policy on `booking_events` (D-076: no booking, message or payment), and the invoker function reads under it. The tenant's owner sees both; the super user sees the audit rows alone. Kept, not worked around.

**What the test suites do to the live log:** every write a probe makes on villa or the platform on service_role is a `system` row ("System deleted the promo villa ten", a super user added and removed). verify and both walks now sweep their own system rows at the end, counted; the 49 that the first runs left were removed by hand.

## D-141 · What is cached, and what is not · **Added 2026-10-21**

**Decision:** three caches, each where the cached thing cannot go stale,
and a list of what stays uncached, after the user asked "do you think we
can apply caching? in any that is applicable. image assets css. api."
and then "implement if what you think would have a positive impact".

1. **Room photos carry `Cache-Control: max-age=31536000`** at upload
   (`PHOTO_CACHE_SECONDS`, `images.ts`), as brand images have since
   D-123. Safe because a photo's path is a UUID written once
   (`upsert: false`): a replaced photo is a new object at a new URL.
   Storage's default was an hour, so every return to the booking page or
   the lightbox re-validated every photo. `tools/photo-cache.mjs` rewrote
   the seven existing objects (same path, same bytes) and reads the
   header back past the CDN.
2. **Tenant pages preconnect to the Storage host** (`preconnect()` in
   `app/t/[tenant]/layout.tsx`): DNS, TCP and TLS are opened before the
   first `<img>` asks. The host alone, which every image URL carries
   already; no key goes with it (rule 2).
3. **A question's embedding is remembered in-process**
   (`packages/rag/src/embed-cache.ts`, `EMBED_CACHE_SIZE` 500, least
   recently used out first), keyed by the text AND the model, so a change
   of `OPENAI_EMBEDDING_MODEL` misses (trap 1). The query side only;
   ingest never reads it. A tenant's suggested questions (D-089) are the
   same text every time, so they hit from the second click. A map, not a
   table: a table any token could read needs a policy and a definer
   (R-22) for a saving an in-process map gives free; each instance warms
   its own.

**Not cached, on purpose:** the answer call (history, the date,
availability; trap 24), availability and quotes (trap 8), the Manage
booking lookups (rate-limited, lockouts), anything read under a tenant
token across requests (a cache keyed by slug alone would hand one role's
data, the sources list, to another), the service worker and the
manifest (`no-cache`, as before), the dashboard JSON (staff want fresh
counts; nobody has found it slow). **Tenant resolution per request**
(`tenant_public()` plus about seven reads on the chat page) is left as
is until measured: a TTL would delay a theme edit or a feature switch,
which the walks check right after the PATCH, and the `TenantContext`
holds a five-minute token that must not be cached. **OpenAI's prompt
caching** is parked: its discount needs a repeated prefix of 1024
tokens, and the prompt's stable part is about 300 before the context,
with the tools block after it; moving the block is a `buildPrompt()`
edit, Rule 1, and the battery cannot run until northwind and harbor are
rebuilt.

**Measured (2026-10-21):** before, a room photo answered
`public, max-age=3600` (brand images a year); after `--apply`, all seven
objects' metadata and their public URLs a year, though the CDN served
the old header for some minutes after the rewrite (the tool's first
read-back said 4 of 7 stale; the check now adds a throwaway query
string). The page's head carries
`<link rel="preconnect" href="https://<project>.supabase.co"/>`. Two
identical turns on alteza: the second logged
`[query] embedding from cache (1 held)`. rag tests 375 (5 new), bookings
133, web 218, typecheck 13/13. No prompt or tool text changed; the
pipeline's reply is the same vector, so retrieval is unchanged.

## D-146 · The staff app's icon is a PNG our route draws, for every tenant · **Added 2026-10-21**

**Decision:** `GET /t/<slug>/app-icon.png?size=192|512|180` always answers
a square PNG, and the manifest and the staff pages' `<head>` point at it.
The user: "current no APP icon when PWA installed".

- **Why there was none:** the manifest named the tenant's logo only when
  it had one, as `sizes: any`, and a logo is a WebP of any shape
  (`resize-image.ts` makes it so). Android's installer wants square PNGs
  at 192 and 512; iOS reads its Home Screen icon from
  `apple-touch-icon`, never from the manifest. Villa, with no logo, had
  no icon at all; alteza's WebP was not one either.
- **With a logo:** fetched from its bucket (5 s limit) and set by `sharp`
  at 70 % of the side on a tile of the theme colour the logo's visible
  pixels contrast with most (panel, accent or ink; alteza's cream mark
  lands on its dark olive accent, a dark mark would land on the panel).
  `sharp` is Next's own image library, now declared on the web app too:
  the same copy from the store, no new download. Next's renderer
  (`next/og`) was tried first and drew the WebP as a blank tile,
  silently, so it keeps only the text case.
- **Without one, or when the logo cannot be fetched or decoded:** the
  business's initial on its accent through `next/og`, the mark
  `BrandMark` draws.
- **Sizes:** an allowlist of three; anything else is 512. The same 512
  serves `maskable`: full-bleed, the mark inside the 40 % safe zone.
  `Cache-Control: public, max-age=3600`, so a brand change reaches the
  icon within the hour (installers re-read on update).
- The response names the tile it chose in `X-App-Icon-Tile`.

**Measured (2026-10-21):** villa and alteza: 192, 512 and 180 all
`image/png` with the right IHDR dimensions; `?size=10000` answers 512;
the admin `<head>` carries `rel="icon"`, `rel="apple-touch-icon"` and the
manifest; alteza's tile `#2d3223 for a logo of #eae2c0`. Typecheck 13/13.
Owed: the user's install on a phone and on Chrome, where the icon is
judged.

**Reverse if:** a tenant wants its icon separate from its logo: then the
platform form takes an icon image and this route serves it, resized,
unchanged otherwise.

**Amended 2026-10-21 (the user: "on header account dropdown, chat, booking and manage booking page should be open a new tab"):** the staff account menu's three guest-page links open in a NEW tab (`target="_blank"`, `rel="noopener"`, a hidden "(opens in a new tab)"): staff look at a guest page beside their work, not instead of it. ## D-148 · Every page says which build it is: the commit and the date, never a number bumped by hand · **Added 2026-10-26**

**Decision:** "Build cd1c21a · 2026-10-26" on every page's foot: the public
footers (the booking page, Manage booking), the chat's fine print, under
the staff sidebar, beside the platform's name, the landing page's footer.
The user: "please add version. so i know im accessing the latest version.
please put it on the best position".

- **The commit, not a number.** A version someone must remember to bump
  says nothing reliable about what is deployed; the short commit and the
  build date do, and change on every deploy by themselves. Vercel sets
  `VERCEL_GIT_COMMIT_SHA`; on a machine `git rev-parse --short HEAD`, and
  a "+" when the tree has uncommitted changes, so a dev build is never
  mistaken for the deploy.
- **Once.** `next.config.mjs` works it out at build time and inlines it as
  `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_VERSION`; `lib/version.ts` reads that and nothing
  else; `components/build-tag.tsx` is the one element. Visible text, never
  a title alone (D-102), so a phone can read it and a person can quote it.
- **Where.** The foot of each page, where a person looks last and nothing
  competes with it: small, muted, tabular digits.

**Measured (2026-10-26):** all eight places read "Build cd1c21a+ ·
2026-10-26" on the dev server (the "+" because the tree was uncommitted),
at 1280 and 375 (`plan/version/*.png`); web 243; typecheck 13/13.

## D-149 · A staff page answers the click before it arrives, and costs fewer round trips to get there · **Added 2026-10-27**

**Decision:** the user: "i feel that app is a bit slow when transitioning
from pages"; then "implement first those who dont have tradeoffs". Four
things, none of which changes what a page shows or who may see it.

- **`loadBranding()` is cached per request** (React `cache()`, like
  `getTenant()` and `loadFeatures()`). The tenant layout and the page it
  wraps both asked, so every staff page paid `tenant_public` three times
  (one of them getTenant()'s); now once.
- **The 404 check runs beside the loads, not before them,** on the 13
  admin pages that have one: `hasApplication()` / `featureOn()` go into
  the page's `Promise.all` and the `notFound()` comes after it. They are
  the same cached questions `loadNavFeatures()` asks, and awaiting them
  first was one serial round trip per page (two on Rooms). Nothing renders
  on a miss, as before.
- **The frame draws the coming page on the click** (`staff-frame.tsx`):
  the clicked link's label as the title and the breadcrumb, the sidebar's
  current mark on it, and `PageBones` in place of the old page, while the
  next page's server render is in flight; the sidebar and the top bar stay
  put. Set in the link's own click (a plain left click only; a link to the
  page shown does nothing), cleared by `useLinkStatus()` when a navigation
  ends without a new page. The new page mounts its own frame, so the state
  leaves with the old one. The same bones the page then shows while it
  checks the session (D-145), so the hand-off moves nothing.
- **`staffClient()` was NOT memoised:** no route asks it twice in one
  request, so there was nothing to save.

**Not a Next loading boundary.** The first version was
`app/t/[tenant]/admin/loading.tsx` with the same skeleton. It streams the
shell at once, which means a page's `notFound()` comes AFTER the status
line: `/t/villa/admin/accommodations` and `/t/nope/admin/bookings`
answered **200** with `<meta name="robots" content="noindex">` and the
not-found page in the stream; with the file moved aside, 404 and 404.
`plan/features-walk.mjs` (4) and `plan/tenant-management-phase4-walk.mjs`
(9) assert a page's 404, and D-127 says a switched-off feature IS a 404.
That is a tradeoff, so it went. The client-side version keeps every status.

**Trap, measured:** the bones were first set from `LinkProgress`'s
`useLinkStatus()` report in an effect. The ring and the bar drew, the bones
never did: a 4-second timeline after the click read ring+bar at 64 ms, no
`.page-pending` in 20 samples, the new page at 1067 ms. A state set from
inside the navigation's optimistic render does not draw until the
transition lands. Set in the click handler itself, it drew in 14 ms.

**Measured (2026-10-27, `plan/page-pending-walk.mjs`, villa, a throwaway
staff member, headless Chrome at 1280, the dev server):** 5/5 twice. On the
click, title "Bookings", breadcrumb "Front desk › Bookings", the sidebar's
current mark on Bookings, `.page-pending .page-bones` present, the sidebar
present, no `.staff-skeleton`: after **14 ms** and **18 ms**; the real
page (no bones, URL moved) after 1483 ms and 1245 ms. Back to Dashboard:
the bones again, no search field or page action left under them. Rooms on
villa and an unknown tenant: HTTP **404 · 404**. Dashboard and Bookings
200. Web tests 243, typecheck clean. The round trips saved are by
construction (one `cache()` and one `Promise.all` per page), not timed:
the dev server's numbers are dominated by compilation.

**Left on the table, each a tradeoff (the user's call):** pinning the
function region to the database's (no `preferredRegion` is set, so every
hop above crosses from Vercel's default region); the session passed from
the server page instead of fetched after mount (one HTTP hop and three
database hops per page, at the cost of the page repeating the route's
check); one SQL function for applications, features and role rows.

**Reverse if:** Next lets a loading boundary carry a page's own status
code; then `loading.tsx` replaces the frame's state, and the walk's check
4 is what proves it safe.

## D-150 · The server code runs where the database is: `preferredRegion = 'sin1'` · **Added 2026-10-27**

**Decision:** one export in `apps/web/app/layout.tsx`, the root: Vercel
runs every page and route handler of this app in Singapore, the Supabase
project's region (the user: "supabase region is in singapore"). Vercel's
default is US East, which put the Pacific in every hop of the chain a
staff page makes (D-149 counts them), and in the chat's too.

  segment configs down the tree (`next/dist/build/utils.js`), so a value on
  the root layout is every segment's unless one overrides it. None does.
- **The dashboard knob is the same decision by hand:** Vercel → Project →
  Settings → Functions → Function Region. The deploy's Functions tab
  shows each function's region; the first deploy after this is where the
  line is checked, because nothing here can reach Vercel.
- **The cost, named:** a visitor far from Singapore reaches the server
  from further away, once per request, against a dozen hops that each got
  shorter. For a Philippine resort's guests and staff there is no cost.

**Measured:** typecheck clean. Not measurable on a machine: the deploy
measures it (the Network tab's RSC request on a staff page change, before
and after). From Manila, three probes of the Supabase REST host took 107,
160 and 188 ms end to end, which is the floor the pinned function's hops
should approach, not the US East round trip.

tenants' staff spread across continents (then the database is what moves).

account, with the owner a Viewer on it and never more (M-021 q1;
plan Rule 9). `tenants.analytics_id` (`schema-analytics.sql`, the 46th
file) is unique across tenants, and `tenant_public()` returns it only
while the switch is on. The switch goes on only with an ID and the
tenant's written-instruction date, `tenants.analytics_instructed_on`
(FR-analytics-028). The FIRST switch-on bumps `policy_version` and stamps
`analytics_since`; a re-enable does not (A-R5). A CSP for the whole app
(R-55, a host allowlist, M-021 q4) allows Google's hosts on the three
measured paths only, and gives the proof viewer `frame-src`. StaffFrame
reloads any document that held gtag.js, so a staff screen never shares a
document with it.

**Amended 2026-10-28 (gate 5, round 2):** from the user's answers (M-021),
Rhea's amendments (M-023) and Sage's review (M-020, S-A1–S-A10). Round 1
bumped the version on every flip, and had no instruction date, no
uniqueness, no `frame-src` and no StaffFrame guard. `plan/analytics.md` § 8
maps each change to its concern.

**Rejected:** the tenant layout as the place (it wraps `/admin/**`).
Consent Mode, basic or advanced (Google code before a choice). One platform
property (GA4 cannot restrict an owner to one tenant's rows, so FR-022
would fail). The Measurement Protocol from the server (a second open
write route, and GA4's sessions and sources would be lost). A nonce CSP for
now (it makes `/` dynamic; R-55 keeps it open). A bump of the version on
every flip (FR-019 says first switch-on and text changes). Link
discipline alone as the staff wall (S-A2: one future `<Link>` breaks it).

**Rests on:** GA4 behaviour nobody has read yet (R-63). The plan's Phase 0
confirms each fact before any code.

lines: a cast is a claim about someone else's JSON. Validating them would be a real
improvement and a real dependency on the hot path; not taken during a port.
+**Amended 2026-10-28 (T-013, deps-upgrade): zod 4, with zod 3's words.**
+Zod 3.25.76 is the last 3.x, and GHSA-mrhx-c7xc-m3w5 (high: an array
+parse keeps an issue for every failing element) is fixed only in 4.6.6.
+So zod is now `^4.6.6` (4.6.7 installed), a major, for a fix 3.x does not
+have. The contract above is unchanged:
+- `typeError(required, invalid)` and `failedWith(words)` in `schemas.ts`
+  say what zod 3's `required_error` / `invalid_type_error` and a refine's
+  message function said.
+- `v3Words`, set ONCE with `z.config({ customError })`, gives zod 3's
+  default wording to every issue no schema names. It has zod 4's lowest
+  precedence, so every written message still wins.
+- Every list a route takes has a `.max()`: zod 4 refuses an over-cap
+  list before parsing one element, and an uncapped list is still parsed
+  whole. Five gained one, at the bound and in the words the package or
+  SQL already used (`rooms` 10, `days` 100, `methods` 5,
+  `cancellation` 5); `rates` 100 is new.
+- `zod/v3` (zod 3's code, shipped inside zod 4) was not used: it is the
+  old parser, without the fix.
+**Measured:** a fixed corpus of 32,673 inputs over all 45 schemas gave
+the same first message on zod 3 and zod 4, the only one `firstError()`
+shows, for every input. The pass/fail answer and the parsed data were
+the same too. 701 inputs differ only after the first issue: zod 4 runs a
+length check on a value that already failed its type, and skips a bound
+after a failed `.int()`. A million empty `rooms`: zod 3 made 2,000,001
+issues in 1,136 ms and +379 MB of heap; zod 4 with the cap made 1 issue
+in 2 ms.
+**Reverse if:** a route needs more than one message from a parse (then
+the later issues matter and differ), or zod 4 changes the precedence
+that lets `v3Words` sit under every written message.

> **What this file is:** the live "where am I / what's next" log for the **build

> **when I sit down to work, what do I do next?**

> re-reading everything.
